subject: A named, stably identified UI state or value that is only compared against itself.
reading: One capture of a UI state: tree, styles, accessibility info, and who wrote each node.
variation: A UI state declared as a variant of another, e.g. dark mode beside light mode.
profile: Declaration of what an observer could see, e.g. whether layout geometry was available.
render document: Serialized markup, applicable CSS, viewport and fonts, portable enough to paint elsewhere later.
semantic snapshot: Normalized, comparable capture: DOM tree, accessible names, applied styles, geometry, source attribution per node.
digest: Hash over one dimension of a capture: structure, semantics, text, style, geometry or component internals.
band: Category of change: accessibility, geometry, design token, content, or anti-aliasing texture; loudest first.
impact: Whether a change affects layout or only paint, independent of the change category.
component hash: Set of hashes covering only the DOM nodes a single component itself produced.
provenance: Which component encloses a rendered node, and which component actually wrote it.
call site: Source file, line and column that created a JSX element, kept on its DOM node.
renderer identity: Hash of every input affecting pixels: engine, platform, scale, fonts, freezing steps, launch flags.
raster: Screenshot image plus a metadata file describing the rendering setup that produced it.
baseline: Stored, previously accepted snapshot a new capture is compared against, per rendering environment.
candidate: The freshly captured side of a comparison, which a person may accept as reference.
verdict: Per-UI-state outcome of a run: unchanged, changed, new, not comparable, or excluded by rule.
ignored: Passed only because declared exclusion rules swallowed every difference; distinct from truly unchanged.
incomparable: Cannot be compared because the two captures came from different rendering setups or observer abilities.
unobserved: Nobody looked; explicitly distinct from having looked and found no change.
not observed: A UI state the run skipped, listed by name with the reason for skipping.
cause: The component whose own content changed, as opposed to things displaced by it.
place: Location inside a UI state given as a DOM subtree path, never a rectangle.
cluster: Secondary changes grouped under one originating change, shown as one item with a count.
docket: Sign-off agenda for a run: originating changes grouped across all UI states, with counts.
ignore: Declared rule excluding a difference by DOM subtree or change shape, with a mandatory reason.
fingerprint: Hash of a difference with position and values stripped, so identical artifacts match anywhere.
sensitivity: Per-UI-state setting choosing which change categories are asserted: strict, layout, or content.
instrument: A controlled comparison varying exactly one factor, like commit or time, holding everything else fixed.
second reading: Deliberately re-capturing the same UI state to test whether it changes on its own.
sweep: A run that captures every UI state twice; the denominator for flakiness rates.
prune: Deleting cache entries whose owner (git, filesystem, process) says they are no longer used.
flake: A UI state that captured inconsistently, then did so a second time when rechecked.
suspect: A UI state that captured differently once; not yet confirmed as nondeterministic.
instability: Disagreement between two captures that should match; a defect to locate, never noise to retry.
stabilization recipe: Named tweaks applied before capture: pause animations, hide caret, await fonts, blank volatile resources.
stabilization: Everything done to an application, from outside it, to make captures deterministic.
intervention: One named tweak applied to a page to make captures deterministic, e.g. pausing animations.
arrival: Whether a UI state has finished loading; still-loading states are refused, not captured.
settled: Finished loading and safe to capture, as opposed to still pending or unknown.
reach: Which UI states and tests a code change could affect, derived from source imports.
closure: Hash over a file and all its transitive dependencies, proving it is unchanged.
seed: Extra changed input fed into test selection: another tool's affected projects, or bumped lockfile packages.
before reach: Files nothing imports but every test depends on: test config, setup, bundler, Node version, CI.
journey: Code regions one test execution entered, across all processes, joined by one opaque trace id.
crossing: One recorded entry of a test into a probed region of source code.
story: Ordered list of code declarations one test case visited, captured only on request.
arrival region: A section of source code with a probe that records when execution enters it.
presence probe: Tiny call inserted before a code region, recording that some test entered it.
execution record: Stored coverage data saying which test files entered which regions of which modules.
source index: Persisted per-file records of a checkout: imports, content hashes, and declared components.
announcement: Signal the application emits at the moment it decides something: location, target, action.
watched run: Long-lived process holding what a test suite emits, queryable while tests are still running.
scenario: Recorded path through named UI states: a precondition, user steps, and each resulting state.
act: One authored step in a recorded user flow, labelled with a stable key.
attention: Which elements a test interacted with, in order, with their authoring component captured beforehand.
presentation graph: Graph of spacing, alignment, containment and repetition relationships between elements in one UI.
presentation finding: A named layout relationship defect, like collapsed separation or an item inconsistent with its peers.
hierarchy contract: Product-declared meaning of spacing relationships, e.g. which gap separates a header from its body.
presentation signal: Summary of layout defects introduced, resolved or persisting, stored without applying any policy.
echo: The same rendered component appearing in several UI states, so its changes count once.
divergence: Same component with same inputs rendering differently at one commit; evidence of nondeterminism.
movement ladder: Ordered explanation of why a component changed: edited, token, upstream, contradicted, or no explanation.
unexplained: A component change with no edit, token or upstream explanation; worth capturing twice.
held: UI states where the same component with same inputs stayed identical: the control group.
approval: A named person's recorded sign-off accepting a new capture; append-only, reversals add rows.
capability: Permission derived from the credential presented; uploading evidence and accepting it are separate permissions.
build: One run's evidence uploaded to the sign-off service for a person to accept or reject.
decision: One person's accept-or-reject answer for one UI state, recorded with their name.
changelog: Why each stored reference image exists: regions, commit, intent and approver, frozen as a copy.
churn: How often a component changed over a time window.
recurrence: How often a UI state proved nondeterministic over a window, per double-capture run.
drift: Movement over time in a value meant to stay fixed, usually a design token.
run report: Versioned output file of a run: every UI state, its outcome, regions, origins, and skips.
quiet run: A run where nothing changed; still recorded because rates need it as a denominator.
collateral: Things that changed only because some other component's content changed.
absorbed: A difference swallowed by a declared exclusion rule, rather than one that never occurred.
enclosure: The component whose boundary contains a rendered node, not necessarily the one that wrote it.
authorship: The component that actually created an element and therefore controls its inputs.
promotion: Replacing the stored reference with an accepted new capture, moving existing evidence only.
parting: The point where two captures, or two execution paths, first differ.
wiring: A component's internal shape as a change category: hooks, wrappers, contexts, keys.
composition: Comparing one run's UI states with each other at one commit, via shared components.
inspection: Checking one stored capture for defects with nothing to compare it against.
standing world: One page kept alive across many UI states, detecting cross-contamination rather than resetting.
isolated reading: Re-capturing a changed UI state on a fresh page to rule out test-order effects.
again: Re-capture on the same page after time passes, checking the UI state agrees with itself.
alone: Re-capture on a fresh page with nothing else loaded, checking for test-order effects.
order-dependent: Outcome that changes depending on which UI states ran earlier on the same page.
realm: An execution environment: product code, browser page, or test driver process.
ledger: Per-rule accounting of what each exclusion or setting matched, including zero matches.
sidecar: JSON metadata file stored next to a screenshot, describing how it was produced.
operator: The person running and configuring the tool, responsible for fixing setup errors.
host: Existing tool already able to show a UI state: Storybook, or a served route.
collector: Pluggable module that enumerates and captures UI states from Storybook or served routes.
change proposal: A pull request or merge request.
sense: Test selection and change-effect analysis: which tests and components a source change affects.
vantage: Background process an agent can query for what a running test suite is emitting.
tribunal: Self-hosted web service where people accept or reject captured UI changes.
eyes: Records which DOM elements a test targets and which React component created them.
wire: Local address where a process under test sends messages for the run that started it.
ioc: Test-only hooks letting modules declare how to reset their state; production code skips them.
distill: Summarizes one test's targeted UI, React update triggers and executed code into simplification opportunities.
session: Runs many UI states in one persistent page and detects cross-contamination between them.
remote: Runs the screenshot renderer or reference image store behind an HTTP endpoint.
observe: Compares two page snapshots or screenshots and returns one comparison result.
event: Library letting application code announce choices, so tests wait instead of guessing timing.
history: Keeps comparison results across runs to answer change-rate, flakiness and token-change questions.
help: MCP server that finds an exported symbol's signature, docs, consumers and usages.
jsx-source: Carries the file and line that wrote each JSX element onto the rendered DOM node.
route-collector: Turns pages an app already serves into UI states to capture.
storybook-collector: Turns a built or served Storybook into a list of UI states to capture.
unit-test: Captures mounted components in Jest, Vitest or Rstest without a browser, painting them later.
vitest-browser: Compares a component to its stored reference image from inside a Vitest browser-mode test.
playwright-test: Adds a visual comparison with source attribution to an existing Playwright test.
png-sharp: Faster PNG decoding through the sharp native library.
editors: VS Code and JetBrains plugins showing, in the gutter, which test cases ran each line.
